---
title: List, filter and search
description: Read the items you need from an instance, a page at a time, narrowed by type, tags and properties, or found by the words they hold.
---

An app reads most of what it shows as a listing. Each operation reads only what your credential can read. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows. To keep a listing so every app shows the same one, [save it as a view](/build/save-a-view), and to list events by the days they fall on, [read a calendar](/build/read-a-calendar).

## List a page at a time

[List items](/api-reference/items/listItems) answers one page and describes every parameter:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --type core.note --tag reading --limit 20
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /items?type=core.note&tags=reading&limit=20
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
  params: { query: { type: "core.note", tags: "reading", limit: 20 } },
});
```

The answer holds the page in `data` and a cursor in `next_cursor`. Send the cursor back as `cursor`, with the same query, for the next page.

Stop only when **`next_cursor` is `null`**: a page can be short, or even empty, and still have more after it. The CLI prints the cursor to send as `more: --cursor <cursor>`.

In the TypeScript SDK, `pages` follows the cursor:

```ts
import { pages } from "@withmarfa/client";

const notes = pages(async (cursor) => {
  const { data, error } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
    params: { query: { type: "core.note", tags: "reading", cursor } },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(error.error.message);
  return data;
});

for await (const row of notes) {
  // Some listings answer { item, metadata } rows.
  const note = "item" in row ? row.item : row;
  console.log(note.properties.title);
}
```

## Narrow a listing

With no parameters, a listing returns the **active items** of every type you can read, in **both tiers**. These parameters narrow it, in any combination:

| Parameter | Keeps |
| --- | --- |
| `type` | Up to 10 types, comma-separated, each with every type beneath it, so `core.file` includes images. A pattern such as `core.*` matches every type under the prefix. |
| `tags` | Items that carry every tag in a comma-separated list. |
| `state` | One state, such as `archived`; a comma-separated list, such as `active,archived`; or `any` on its own. |
| `tier` | `library` or `feed` items. |
| `source` | Items one writer created. |
| `occurred_after`, `occurred_before` | Items whose `occurred_at` falls between two times. |
| `backref[<edge type>]` | Items an edge from another item points to: `backref[parent-of]=<id>` lists a task's subtasks. |

A list's blank entries and repeats count for nothing. `include=metadata` or `include=edges` adds each item's tags and extensions, or its edges, to the answer.

## Filter by properties

A `filter` narrows by the values items hold. It's one or more conditions of the form `<field> <operator> <value>`, **joined by `AND` or by `OR` (not both)**, and it can name a property as `properties.<name>`. This finds the tasks of high or urgent priority:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --type core.task \
  --filter 'properties.priority eq "high" OR properties.priority eq "urgent"'
```

```bash tab="HTTP"
curl -G "$MARFA_API_URL/items" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "type=core.task" \
  --data-urlencode 'filter=properties.priority eq "high" OR properties.priority eq "urgent"'
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/items", {
  params: {
    query: {
      type: "core.task",
      filter: 'properties.priority eq "high" OR properties.priority eq "urgent"',
    },
  },
});
```

Strings go in double quotes. **Inside a string, write `\"` for a double quote and `\\` for a backslash**; any other backslash stays as typed. A query string needs the filter URL-encoded, as `--data-urlencode` does. A filter can test tags and an item's own fields too, with operators such as `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `lt`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `exists` and `not_exists`.

To find items where a property is missing or `null`, use **`not_exists`**: Marfa refuses a comparison with `null`.

**`status_group`** tests the group of an item's [status word](/catalog/field-kinds), so one filter spans types whose words differ. `status_group neq "completed" AND status_group neq "canceled"` finds everything not yet done. It takes `eq`, `neq`, `exists` and `not_exists`, with `not_started`, `in_progress`, `completed` or `canceled`. An item whose type has no status field, or whose word its type doesn't declare, is in no group, so only `not_exists` selects it.

**`properties.<field>.<member>`** finds an item by any entry of a list: `properties.emails.value eq "priya@example.com"` finds a person by any of their email addresses. It takes `eq` only, and exactly two names after `properties`. It skips an item whose field isn't a list of objects holding the member.

Any other form of either term is refused `400 validation_error`. Both work in a search, a [saved view](/build/save-a-view) and a working copy. The [search and filters](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/search-and-filters.md) chapter of the contract has the whole grammar.

## Sort

A listing comes **newest first**: by `created_at`, or, for a listing of the bin alone (`state=trashed`), by `trashed_at`. `sort` orders it by `created_at`, `updated_at`, `occurred_at` or a property, and `direction` takes `asc` or `desc`. This lists tasks due before October 21, soonest first:

```bash tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
curl -G "$MARFA_API_URL/items" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "type=core.task" \
  --data-urlencode 'filter=properties.due_at lt "2026-10-21T00:00:00Z"' \
  --data-urlencode "sort=properties.due_at" --data-urlencode "direction=asc"
```

The CLI's `--sort` takes the three times but not a property. Items that lack the property come last, whichever the direction.

## Find what changed

To catch up with what changed since you last read, list with `updated_after` set to the latest `updated_at` you hold:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items list --updated-after 2026-10-09T23:50:54.460Z
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /items?updated_after=2026-10-09T23:50:54.460Z
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

The bound includes items changed at that instant, so **skip the ones you already hold by `id`**: items written together share an `updated_at`. This listing is always oldest change first, and refuses any other `sort` or `direction`. A listing **can't report a purged item**: to hear of every change, purges included, follow the event stream as [Keep a copy in sync](/build/keep-in-sync) shows.

## Search

[Search items](/api-reference/search/searchItems) finds items by the words they hold, best match first unless you sort it:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa search tide --type core.note
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /search?q=tide&type=core.note
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.GET("/search", {
  params: { query: { q: "tide", type: "core.note" } },
});
```

Each entry in `data` holds the `item`, its `metadata`, a `relevance_score`, and a `snippet_html` showing where the text matched, such as `High <mark>tide</mark> at six`. The snippet escapes the item's text and marks each match, so **it's safe to show as HTML**.

**Every word** in `q` must match, in any order, in the item's [searched fields](/catalog/items#searched-fields), such as a file's [extracted text](/build/handle-files#find-a-file-by-its-text), or its tags. Words match by their stem, so `tides` finds `tide`, and the last word matches as a prefix, so a search run on each keystroke finds results as someone types.

Put a query in double quotes to match a phrase. A search takes a listing's narrowing parameters too, `filter`, `updated_after` and `updated_before` among them, so words and conditions work in one call. **A search never matches an item in the bin**, whatever `state` it names.

### Sort a search

`sort` orders a search by `relevance`, the default, or by `created_at`, `updated_at`, `occurred_at` or a property, as a listing sorts. `direction` takes `asc` or `desc`, and under `relevance`, `desc` puts the best match first. This finds notes about tides changed since October 19, latest first:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa search tide --type core.note --updated-after 2026-10-19T00:00:00Z --sort updated-at
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /search?q=tide&type=core.note&updated_after=2026-10-19T00:00:00Z&sort=updated_at
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

Unlike a listing, **`updated_after` doesn't set the order of a search**, so it works with any `sort`, and ties go by `id`.

A cursor works only with the query that gave it: sent with another `sort`, `direction`, `source`, `updated_after` or `updated_before`, it's refused `400 validation_error`. A search reads **at most the first 10,000 hits** of its ranking, so narrow one that would reach further.

## Count items

[Get item counts](/api-reference/items/getItemStats) counts the items a listing would match, by state or, with `by=type`, by type:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items stats --by type
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /items/stats?by=type
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

```json title="Response" status="200"
{ "core.event": 2, "core.note": 10, "core.task": 5 }
```

Over HTTP, a count takes a listing's narrowing parameters, such as `tags=reading`. Unlike a listing, **it includes every state unless you name one**, the bin included.

## When a query is refused

Marfa refuses a query it can't answer exactly, rather than answer a different one:

- **A parameter the operation doesn't take**, such as `tag` for `tags`, answers `400 validation_error` and lists it in `details.unknown_parameters`. Marfa ignores any parameter that starts with `_`, so use that prefix for your own.
- **A `type`, `tags`, `state`, `source` or `filter` sent empty**, or as a list of blank entries, answers `400 validation_error`, so an unset variable doesn't read everything.
- **More than 10 types, or `any` beside another state,** answers `400 validation_error`.
- **A `type` nothing registers** answers `400 unknown_type`.
- **A `type` you can't read** answers `403 type_not_permitted`.

The rules behind this guide are in the [search and filters](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/search-and-filters.md) chapter of the contract.
